eval_instructions: Run these against a real agent project that has already been through a365-setup and make-a365-agent (so a Blueprint and Agent Identity exist). Google ADK on Vertex AI Agent Engine is the implemented platform. Verify every generated file carries the marker comment 'A365 Security — added by instrument-security skill'. Verify no credential is ever written into source. A run is only successful if the smoke test shows a benign turn allowed AND a known-bad turn blocked with a readable reason.

evals.description: Happy path — Python Google ADK agent with an existing Blueprint and Agent Identity
evals.expected_output: The skill loads the detection cache, confirms the Blueprint + Agent Identity exist, asks for Defender environment / fail mode / hook selection, creates the platform-agnostic security package plus the google_adk adapter, composes the four ADK callbacks without replacing existing ones, stamps DEFENDER_* into .env, forwards them in deploy.py, compiles, then smoke-tests one benign and one known-bad turn.
expectations: Phase 0.1: Workspace triage runs; .a365-workspace-detection.local.json is read
Phase 0.2: Hard stop if the detection cache is missing — a365-setup is run rather than inventing defaults
Phase 0.3: a365.generated.config.json is read; agentBlueprintId and agenticAppId are extracted
Phase 0.3: Missing agenticAppId is surfaced with the blueprint auth-mode fallback offered, not silently ignored
Phase 0.5: INTERACTION — Defender environment asked (dev/staging/prod)
Phase 0.5: INTERACTION — fail mode asked, with the operational consequence of each option stated
Phase 0.5: INTERACTION — inspection points asked, defaulting to all four
Phase 1: Platform detected as Google ADK from agentStack/google-adk imports
Phase 2: httpx, msal, azure-identity verified or installed; existing pinned versions are NOT changed
Phase 3: security/ package created with config.py, entra_auth.py, ai_session.py, defender_client.py
Phase 3: security/adapters/google_adk.py created — platform-specific code isolated from the core
Phase 3: Every generated file carries the marker comment 'A365 Security — added by instrument-security skill'
Phase 4: All four ADK callbacks wired via secure_agent_callbacks
Phase 4: Pre-existing callbacks are passed through and preserved, not replaced
Phase 5: DEFENDER_* keys appended to .env without duplicating existing keys
Phase 5: deploy.py forwards DEFENDER_* through env_vars, and the user is told deployed runtimes do not read .env
Phase 6: resourceConsents checked; missing prevention resource is surfaced as a GA handoff, never self-granted
Phase 7: Project compiles / imports cleanly
Phase 8: Benign turn allowed — one verdict logged per enabled hook
Phase 8: Known-bad turn blocked with reason and diagnostics surfaced to the user
Phase 9: Summary states endpoint, auth mode, identity seen by the webhook, fail mode consequence, and per-hook latency

evals.prompt: Add defender prevention to this agent
evals.description: Idempotency — re-run against an already-instrumented agent
evals.expected_output: The skill detects the existing security package and callback wiring, reports that prevention is already in place, and makes no duplicate edits. Configuration questions already answered in .env are reported rather than re-asked.
expectations: Existing security/ package is detected and not overwritten
secure_agent_callbacks is not applied a second time
DEFENDER_* keys already present in .env are not duplicated
Questions with values already in .env are skipped and the found values reported
No packages are reinstalled and no pinned versions are altered
The run ends with a clear 'already wired' summary rather than a no-op silence

evals.prompt: Add security hooks to this agent
evals.description: Unsupported platform — a .NET or Node.js agent that is not Google ADK
evals.expected_output: The skill detects that no adapter exists for the platform and stops cleanly, explaining that the platform-agnostic core is reusable but the hook bridge is missing. No partial wiring is left behind.
expectations: Platform detection identifies the stack as one without an implemented adapter
The skill stops before creating any files
The message names the platform and states that an adapter under security/adapters/ is required
No packages are installed and no source file is modified
The user is not told the agent is protected

evals.description: Prerequisite missing — no Agent 365 registration in the workspace
evals.expected_output: With agent code present but no fresh detection cache, the skill runs a365-setup to register the agent and write the cache, then continues. With no agent code at all, it hard-stops and points at make-a365-agent.
expectations: Agent code present + stale/missing cache → a365-setup is run to completion, then the skill resumes
No agent code → hard stop naming /agent365:make-a365-agent
No file is edited and no package installed before the cache exists
Default cache values are never invented

evals.prompt: Instrument security for this agent, and block anything Defender flags even if the service is down
evals.description: Fail-closed selection is honored end to end
evals.expected_output: DEFENDER_FAIL_MODE=closed is stamped, the client returns block=true when no verdict is obtained, and the block message distinguishes 'validation unavailable' from 'content flagged as malicious'.
expectations: Phase 0.5: fail-closed is recorded and DEFENDER_FAIL_MODE=closed written to .env
The decision model blocks when the webhook errors, times out, or returns 4xx/5xx
The unavailable-service block message does not claim the content was malicious
The evaluated flag distinguishes a real allow from a masked failure
Phase 9: summary states plainly that a Defender outage will block agent actions

evals.prompt: Add prevention but only on tool calls
evals.expected_output: Only the tool inspection points are wired; agent-level callbacks are passed through untouched. DEFENDER_HOOKS reflects the subset and the validator requires only the enabled hooks.
expectations: DEFENDER_HOOKS=before_tool,after_tool written to .env
before_agent_callback and after_agent_callback are passed through unwrapped
toolRequest and toolResponse activities are built; agentRequest/agentResponse are not required
Phase 9: summary states which inspection points are NOT covered and what that means
